notes: Spelling-to-sound rules of German, applied in order to a lower-case word after its umlauts are written out (ü → ue, from umlautSpelling.json). Two spellings of one pronunciation get one key: Donnerstag and donastag → donastak. Upper-case letters are sound symbols that stand for a whole digraph. Vowels are kept, so words that differ in a vowel (Dienstag, Donnerstag) keep different keys. context (all listed must hold): wordEnd — at the end of the word; beforeConsonantOrEnd — followed by a consonant or the end of the word; afterVowel — preceded by a vowel; laterSyllable — preceded by a consonant that follows a vowel, so not in the first syllable. The vocalic r (-er → a) is unstressed, so it applies only in a later syllable: Donnerstag → donastak, but Berg, Erbe keep their r. Vowel length is kept where the spelling marks it (ie, a lengthening h, a doubled vowel → a colon), so Miete and Mitte stay apart; the lengthening h counts only before a consonant or at the end: mehr = Meer, but Mäher keeps its h.
